reviews.comment: His accent is so heavy, that even I, a trilingual Asian grad student, can barely understand his English. And he's really picky about such weird things, like students exiting the class to use the bathroom etc.

Was doing well in this class, then the final was 40% while covering the 5 hardest units, which dropped my grade, which is crazy how the entire course is easy/manageable until the very end. Lectures were boring and hard to understand due to language barrier, but Prof and TA were nice, easy graders. Complex Derivatives and Linear algebra concepts.

I thought he was a solid option for ECON 323. His exams were very similar to the practice multiple choice and homework. His exam reviews at the end of class were extremely helpful and told us what will be on the exam. His extra credit policy is great, so make sure you have perfect attendance to get all the bonus points.

Huge language barrier - it was so difficult to make out what he was saying most of the time, making the material hard to grasp. It is a calculus heavy class, so it's going to be somewhat challenging, but the hw's are helpful for the exams. The TA is also very helpful and lenient in grading. He takes attendance, but doesn't harm your grade.

The accent does make it hard to understand, but he clearly knows what he is talking about and is very kind. It is a very hard class, but he understands that. There are lots of extra credit opportunities and the tests are very similar to the homework and the practice MC he posts. It is hard, but Tian overall does a good job.

Professors accent was very tough to understand. Practice questions had wrong answers. I basically had to teach myself this class and had to take private tutoring for it. Material itself is difficult and the professors strong accent did not make it any easier. Would not recommend taking.

The hardest part of this class is the language barrier. It takes a few weeks to be able to fully understand what he is saying, but once you do, you just have to study. He gives a few extra credit points based on your attendance throughout the semester. This class with any prof is hard, so it is up to you to study and practice outside of lectures.
